correctness.rationale: For multiplicities m_j, removing required copies yields P(m_{j_i}>=r_i all)=p(n-s)/p(n) exactly. Hardy–Ramanujan ratios with r_i~x_i sqrt(n) give independent rate-c j exponential limits. The uniform bound p(n-s)/p(n)<=C exp(-delta s/sqrt(n)), obtained by splitting s<=n/2 from s>n/2, yields uniform L1 control <=C/[delta(J+1)] for the weighted tail. This justifies convergence of the infinite numerator; Erdos–Lehner gives L_n/(sqrt(n)log n)->1/(2c), so Slutsky yields Z. Telescoping 1/[j(j+1)], square-sum 2zeta(2)-3, and gamma ratios give all constants. Independently checked 432 exact joint-tail identities for n=1..16 and the three smallest part sizes, and numerical Gamma/product comparisons at four t values. These finite checks do not prove classical partition inputs or the weak limit.

originality.rationale: Dawsey–Russell–Urban 2022 introduce exactly these normalized polynomial integrals, prove density, and discuss fixed-length average monotonicity. They do not establish the random fixed-size, logarithmically rescaled integral weak limit in the inspected full-text sections. Hardy–Ramanujan, Erdős–Lehner, and Fristedt multiplicity laws are credited, not repackaged as discoveries; their combination requires an explicit uniform weighted-tail bound and normalization.
